deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 17% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: sales × its 3-year median free-cash margin (12%), because current free cash flow is negative). For comparison, sales grew 11% last year; 1%/yr over 3 years — the market expects faster growth than the company has recently delivered.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 30% — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $30 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 34% (3 years ago 43%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $1.4B, down 2% from a year ago — about 15% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $714M, down 1% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 1%/yr over 3 years and 6%/yr over 5 years.

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $1.4B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($823M buybacks + $611M dividends) = 3.3% of the company's market value. Share count down 1.2% from a year ago (buybacks outpacing stock pay).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $16.69, up 0% in 90 days; 1 analyst raised, 4 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $14.98, up 1% in 90 days; 5 analysts raised, 4 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Intelligent Devices 47% of sales, up 12%; Software & Control 32% of sales, up 19%; Lifecycle Services 21% of sales, down 12%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.sub: +16% vs a year ago · $10.76 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 16% vs sales 8% (latest quarter vs a year earlier): profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 8 quarters running by about 8%, yet the stock fell after 4 of them: beats are already expected.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.sub: latest quarter +8% vs a year earlier · 12-month sales $9.0B
tiles.read: Latest quarter: sales up 8% vs a year earlier but slowing (from 12% two quarters ago): the fastest growth may be behind it.
tiles.explain: Headline: sales over the last 12 months vs the 12 months before. Bars: each quarter's sales vs the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $23 of operating profit, about the same as a year ago.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 36× last year's profit (higher than 65% of the last 5 years); only 23× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Feb 4; analysts expect EPS of $3.00, up 9% from a year ago. It usually moves about 9% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.
